consentScope: Internal repository example and anonymized migration evidence; no external adopter claim is made.

source.workload: Effect composition, Stream transformation, runtime execution, and package-entrypoint rollback

migration.includes: installing the local beta, strict typecheck, execution, beta /next rollback, downloading published stable v1, and stable rollback execution

checks: v2 package root strict typecheck and execution

negativeFindings: The static migration analyzer correctly reports no v1 imports because the baseline already uses /next; package-root promotion therefore requires installed-package type and execution checks rather than import counting alone.
The initial migration run used the local beta tarball; a separate post-publication follow-up repeated the checks against the npm registry tarball after next became available.
This small deterministic core example does not measure cancellation, concurrency, retained memory, latency, or HTTP behavior.
rollbackPath: Change the import from brass-runtime to brass-runtime/next inside the beta, or pin npm:brass-runtime@1.22.0 and retain /next; both rollback paths passed strict types and identical execution results.
limitations: This is an internal deterministic example, not an independent external production workload.
The run proves one Effect and one Stream program and does not represent the full core API.
The initial measurement used a local candidate; registry publication and the later public-tarball replay are separate, timestamped evidence.
The published-v1 rollback was downloaded from npm during this run, but long-term registry availability is outside this evidence.
CPU, memory, latency, retention, upgrade lag, and operational reliability are outside this migration record.
reproduce: node scripts/analyze-v2-migration.mjs --json examples/v2-preview; npm run validate:v2-beta -- --version 2.0.0-beta.0; npm run validate:example:v2-core -- --report artifacts/stability/v2-core-lighthouse-local-2026-09-20.json
